item.text: {"question_id":"2B.1","answer":"For the 2023 period, López Obrador’s government demonstrably used diplomatic authority and formal multilateral channels to pursue peaceful alternatives where international conflicts presented such opportunities. Mexico advocated dialogue, preventive diplomacy, confidence-building, mediation, and a UN-linked caucus for Russia–Ukraine; it also participated in Colombia’s peace dialogue and hosted Venezuela negotiations (BATCH-0045-E012; BATCH-0048-E014). Mexico condemned Russia’s invasion while maintaining neutrality and refusing sanctions, although this policy strained relations with Washington (BATCH-0042-E007). The evidence establishes formal diplomatic initiatives and positions, but not that the proposed Russia–Ukraine caucus was created, that these efforts produced settlement, or that internal cabinet or legislative deliberation preceded any authorization of international force. The supplied record does not document López Obrador authorizing or supporting international force during the period, so the specific pre-force test is only partially observable.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014","BATCH-0042-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E007","BATCH-0045-E012","BATCH-0048-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence documents diplomatic advocacy, negotiation roles, and formal positions, but not implementation or successful outcomes for every proposal.","The supplied record provides little evidence of cabinet or legislative consideration of alternatives and does not establish any 2023 authorization or support for international force by López Obrador.","Domestic security militarization evidence was excluded because it concerns internal public security rather than this international-force question."],"corrections_made":["Removed domestic militarization evidence as outside the scope of 2B.1 absent a demonstrated international-conflict connection.","Removed the unsupported claim that neutrality was an attempted alternative to force requiring a settlement outcome.","Retained the supported finding that neutrality strained relations with Washington, while presenting it as a qualification rather than proof of failed peaceful diplomacy."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen only if additional supplied-period evidence identifies an international force decision, formal cabinet or legislative deliberation, or implementation and outcomes of the proposed diplomatic initiatives."]}
